o.norm: Consonants from the same code group separated by W or H are treated as one.
From http://www.archives.gov/research_room/genealogy/census/soundex.html: Ashcraft is coded A-261 (A, 2 for the S, C ignored, 6 for the R, 1 for the F). It is not coded A-226.

i.norm:
Verifies the H/W rule: when H or W appears between two consonants that share the same Soundex digit, those consonants are treated as one and only encoded once.

Reference: http://www.archives.gov/research_room/genealogy/census/soundex.html

Example breakdown for "Ashcraft":

  • A – kept as the initial letter
  • S – digit 2
  • H – ignored (H/W rule)
  • C – digit 2, same as S → suppressed (adjacent-duplicate rule)
  • R – digit 6
  • A – vowel (digit 0) → not encoded
  • F – digit 1
  • T – digit 3, but the code is already 4 characters → truncated
Result: A261 (not A226, which would be wrong if C were encoded independently).
"Ashcraft" and "Ashcroft" differ only in the vowel between r and f, but vowels are not encoded after the first letter, so both yield A261.
"yehudit" and "yhwdyt" demonstrate the same rule with W: Y is kept as initial; H and W are both ignored; the remaining consonants D and T share a code, collapsing further – result is Y330.
